release_all() now returns only genuinely-held, non-expired paths (src/lease.rs). It reads via the new peek() instead of list(), so GC no longer unlinks expired locks mid-iteration and makes release() report Ok(None) as a release. The agent's own expired lock files are still swept from disk (no leak) but are unlinked directly rather than through release(), so they do not appear in the report or in the pact-rnc.13 event log either. Test: release_all_omits_expired_leases_but_still_sweeps_them.

PARTIALLY addressed, closing in favour of the precisely-scoped follow-up. acquire_many landed and is verified: acquiring [new.rs, shared.rs] where another agent holds shared.rs exits 2, leaves the victim's claim intact, and leaves NO stray new.rs lock — so an agent can now atomically claim a module and its registration line when that line is free. What it does NOT fix is the bead's larger complaint: when the registration line is owned by someone else, the new file still is not compiled, so its owner cannot cargo build or cargo test their own work. lease-fix hit exactly that this round and had to use the copy-the-crate workaround the bead complains about. That residue is pact-v66, which is scoped to it precisely; keeping both open would be two overlapping beads for one problem.

Fixed in 763e209 with regression tests in both modules. The .pact/-creating-on-read half was real and confirmed: log/lease ls/agents all went through repo::pact_dir which create_dir_all's, so a pure read left state behind in a repo that had never used pact. Added repo::pact_dir_path for read paths; verified that log/lease ls/agents now create nothing while lease acquire still does. The other half of the bead was already fine: a corrupt events.jsonl line is skipped (verified: garbage line ignored, valid event shown, exit 0) and a missing bd degrades to a warning rather than failing the command.
